items.title: Automate FortiManager with Python objects
items.text: pyfortinet is a Python library for the FortiManager JSON-RPC API. Work with addresses, groups, services, policies, and other supported resources as Python objects. The library handles session authentication, request construction, and typed GET responses.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• High-level configuration models with Pydantic validation and API field aliases.
  • Synchronous and asynchronous clients with consistent object operations.
  • ADOM workspace locking and connection cleanup.
  • Background task polling with progress callbacks.
  • Dictionary requests and low-level clients for endpoints without a model.

Coverage is evolving. Check the code reference for available models and the target firmware's API reference for supported fields. Direct FortiGate connections, token/SAML authentication, and workflow session approval automation are not implemented.

items.title: Start with your task
items.text:
Goal Read Install and connect Quickstart Translate familiar JSON-RPC operations into Python API concepts Manage objects, mappings, locks, and tasks How-tos Find a resource by domain Object guides Use addresses, services, VIPs, and IP pools Firewall families Configure client behavior Advanced usage Contribute or verify an implementation Developer guide

The code reference is generated from the library's docstrings and includes class and method examples. The user guide builds on that reference with complete workflows; the developer guide covers implementation and verification.

items.title: Developer guide
items.text: This guide covers contributing models, maintaining the clients, and verifying changes. For application examples, start with the user guide.

items.title: Set up a development environment
items.text:
Fork and clone the repository, then run these commands from its root:

git clone https://github.com/YOURFORK/pyfortinet.git
cd pyfortinet
uv sync --locked
uv run pytest tests/unit
uv run invoke --list

uv installs the project in editable mode and includes the default development dependency group. Use uv sync when intentionally changing dependencies and include the updated uv.lock. Keep the published dev extra and development dependency group aligned.

The Flit build backend and pip development extra are also supported:

python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

Preserve the project's Python 3.9 minimum version. Follow the existing module structure and keep synchronous and asynchronous behavior consistent.

items.title: Verify changes
items.text:
Run focused unit tests during development. For client behavior changes, run the unit suite; for HTTP timeout or transport changes, also run the loopback transport tests:

uv run pytest tests/unit
uv run pytest tests/transport

Check changed Python files with uv run ruff check <files> and uv run ruff format --check <files>. For broader checks, use uv run pre-commit run --files <files> and inspect any changes made by hooks.

Default uv run pytest and uv run invoke test select offline checks. Selecting tests explicitly also includes live tests. Read the testing guide and lab setup guide before an authorized live run.

items.title: Preview and build documentation
items.text:
uv run invoke docs-serve
uv run invoke docs

Documentation builds require Python 3.11 or later. The library and its runtime dependencies continue to support Python 3.9. On Python 3.9/3.10, the development extra and group omit Zensical and its Python handler. Use a separate clone or virtual environment with Python 3.11+ for docs; for example, run uv sync --locked --python 3.11 in a dedicated checkout. The pip alternative is python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt using Python 3.11+.

The Invoke tasks first run the independent docs/gen_ref_pages.py generator, then invoke zensical serve or zensical build --strict. Run them from the repository root. The generator writes ignored Markdown under docs/reference/, preserves the published module paths and identifiers, and removes stale generated pages after source files are renamed or removed. It refuses to overwrite Markdown it does not own. Restart docs-serve after adding, renaming, or removing source modules so the generated page list and navigation are refreshed.

For a direct build without Invoke:

uv run python docs/gen_ref_pages.py
uv run zensical build --strict

Keep mkdocs.yml: Zensical supports that configuration format. This project uses the modern theme variant. The classic variant is available for sites that prefer the previous Material appearance; it is not required for this project.

Both variants share the same HTML structure. Changing the variant does not change page URLs, API identifiers, Python requirements, or the publishing workflow. The project's custom CSS still applies, but check desktop and mobile layouts after theme changes or upgrades because visual styling can differ. See the Zensical theme variant guidance.

Search, cross-references, section indexes, and literate navigation use Zensical's compatibility implementations; gen-files is no longer used. The old Invoke task names mkdocs and mkdocs-serve remain aliases. The old --push-to-github flag is removed; local documentation commands do not deploy.

items.title: GitHub Pages
items.text:
The documentation workflow builds source on Python 3.11 and validates pull requests. Pushes to master, and manual runs selecting master, publish the generated site/ contents to the gh-pages branch. Pull requests and manual runs on other branches only build and test; they cannot execute the credential or publication steps. Publication preserves the branch history while replacing obsolete generated files. The publishing action adds .nojekyll to bypass Jekyll.

gh-pages remains generated output, not a source checkout. GitHub's branch-based Pages workflow publishes that branch. Keep the github-pages environment restricted to gh-pages; the source build job does not enter that environment or deploy an artifact directly from master.

Configure the repository before publishing:

  1. In Settings > Pages > Build and deployment, select Deploy from a branch, then gh-pages and /(root). Do not select GitHub Actions for this branch-output workflow.
  2. In Settings > Environments > github-pages, keep the existing gh-pages deployment rule.
  3. Create a dedicated SSH deploy key following the publishing action's key setup instructions. Add its public key under Settings > Deploy keys with Allow write access. Store its private key under Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Repository secrets as DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY. Keep the key files outside the repository and never include the private key in logs or commits. A deploy key grants write access to this repository, not just gh-pages; repository rules must permit its publishing push.
  4. If Actions are restricted, allow actions/checkout, astral-sh/setup-uv, and peaceiris/actions-gh-pages. No broader default GITHUB_TOKEN write permission is needed.

A deploy key is used because GitHub documents that pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger a Pages build. This workflow makes a normal authenticated push, allowing GitHub's Pages publisher to deploy from the permitted branch. See GitHub's publishing-source documentation. Remote Pages settings and credentials are not changed by editing or locally testing this workflow.

items.title: Documentation sources
items.text:
Maintain both documentation layers:

  • User pages explain workflows using high-level objects, prerequisites, and expected results.
  • Developer pages explain implementation, testing, schema sources, and verification limits.
  • Google-style docstrings describe classes and methods with concise examples. Zensical renders the code reference with mkdocstrings; do not maintain a separate copy of the reference.

When public behavior changes, update the relevant examples and docstrings together. Use the API object guide to add a model. Keep raw request construction in implementation or extension examples where it is needed to explain unsupported functionality.

items.title: Build a package locally
items.text:
uv build

Building does not publish a release. Publishing packages and deploying documentation are separate maintainer operations.

items.title: Implementing API objects
items.text: High-level models translate FortiManager resources into validated Python objects. Read the relevant implementation and tests before adding a route. Check Fortinet documentation for the target FMG firmware and managed FortiOS version; record the source and verification limits.

items.title: Choose the domain and base class
items.text:
Place a model in the module matching its API domain. Firewall models live in pyfortinet/fmg_api/firewall/; export public classes through its explicit __all__ in __init__.py. Keep shared normalization in _values.py and literal choices in types.py. Import literal choices from firewall.types and PORT_RANGE_TYPE from firewall.service; the firewall package root also supports explicit imports of these aliases for compatibility, such as from pyfortinet.fmg_api.firewall import PROTOCOL. Its __all__ exposes classes only.

Use FMGObject for configuration resources and FMGExecObject for execution operations. The base classes provide client binding and operation delegation. Keep transport handling in the synchronous and asynchronous clients; share pure request or normalization helpers where useful.

items.title: Define fields, aliases, and identity
items.text:
The following is an illustrative template, not an implemented FortiManager endpoint:

from typing import Optional

from pydantic import AliasChoices, Field

from pyfortinet.fmg_api import FMGObject


class ExampleObject(FMGObject):
    """Illustrative configuration model.

    Attributes:
        name: Object name used for item operations.
        display_name: Optional descriptive name.
    """

    _url = "/pm/config/{scope}/obj/example/{entry}"
    _master_keys = {"entry": "name"}

    name: Optional[str] = None
    display_name: Optional[str] = Field(
        None,
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("display-name", "display_name"),
        serialization_alias="display-name",
    )

_master_keys maps URL placeholders to model fields; it is a dictionary, not a list. Match the documented API identity. Most model fields, including identity fields on collection models, should default to None so collection GETs, partial replies, and partial updates work. An item operation still requires enough information to identify its target. Require a field at construction only when the model cannot represent a valid supported operation without it.

Optional[str] alone allows null values but does not make a Pydantic 2 field optional at construction. Supply a default, usually None, when omission is supported.

Accept Python names and API aliases with AliasChoices and serialize with the API spelling. High-level writes use model_dump(by_alias=True, exclude_none=True); they do not exclude every explicit default or unchanged field. Avoid injecting device defaults into partial writes.

Use Field(..., exclude=True) or an optional excluded field for URL-only parameters and response metadata that must not appear in configuration payloads. Follow existing model conventions and the firmware reference rather than assuming all returned attributes are writable.

items.title: Construct URLs and scopes
items.text:
get_url(method=...) is a method, not a property. The default implementation replaces {scope} with global or adom/<name>, resolves URL fields, and handles terminal selectors according to the operation. Inspect existing models and request tests before overriding it.

Directly constructed models have no scope unless fmg_scope is supplied. High-level client operations supply the selected connection scope when needed. Explicit object scope takes precedence. Returned models retain request scope and URL-only parent fields so later updates and refreshes can reach the same resource.

For package-scoped objects, follow Policy, whose URL includes {adom}, {pkg}, and {policy} and maps the policy selector to policyid. Keep pkg out of the configuration payload. Do not replace get_url with a property or assume every route uses a terminal name selector.

_version is descriptive metadata; it does not currently enforce minimum firmware versions.

items.title: Validate and serialize values
items.text:
Use Pydantic validators for supported normalization, such as API integer choices to Python literals. Map values according to the firmware schema; do not infer an enumeration from an unrelated endpoint. Keep invalid input visible as a validation error.

When an API field references other objects by name, accept the supported names or model types and serialize references as name arrays. Passing a referenced model must not implicitly create it. Use separate nested models when mapping fields differ from parent fields.

Preserve the distinction between an unset collection (None, omitted from writes) and an explicit empty collection ([], sent to the API). Keep synchronous and asynchronous behavior consistent, including aliases and normalization.

items.title: Verify an implementation
items.text:
Add offline regression tests in the matching tests/unit/ domain. Cover construction with Python names and API aliases, normalization, serialization, URL assembly, scope, partial responses, and meaningful invalid inputs. Mock external transport for client behavior. Check both clients when the behavior affects request handling.

Live verification is separate and requires authorization. Register cleanup before writes, refuse pre-existing test resources, and keep each test independent. See the testing guide for fixtures, baseline requirements, and cleanup limitations.

items.title: Document and review
items.text:
Use Google-style class and method docstrings with concise, valid examples. Explain identifiers, URL-only fields, supported operations, and relevant serialization behavior. Add user-facing workflows to the user guide and schema or firmware verification details to the developer guide.

Run the focused tests, Ruff checks for changed Python files, and uv run invoke docs (Python 3.11+). Document unavailable firmware references or device verification explicitly. Do not claim runtime support merely because a schema-backed model validates locally.

items.title: Lab setup for testing
items.text: Offline unit tests and loopback transport tests do not require a FortiManager lab. Live tests require an explicitly authorized, disposable environment and a reviewed set of operations. See the testing guide for configuration and commands.

items.title: Prepare a lab
items.text:
Use dedicated FortiManager and FortiGate instances that can be restored to a known baseline. Virtual machines are suitable; on Windows, Hyper-V checkpoints can support restoration. Ensure the test machine can reach FortiManager and the lab devices can communicate as required.

Record the expected firmware, ADOMs, device names, serial numbers, permitted operations, and baseline restore procedure before running live scenarios. A separate ADOM does not isolate administrator changes, device lifecycle operations, or configuration installations.

items.title: Configure FortiManager
items.text:
A dedicated test ADOM with normal workspace mode is recommended. Confirm that the test account has JSON-RPC API access and permissions for the selected operations. Workflow session creation and approval are not covered by the client locking helpers.

Store credentials locally in the gitignored private/lab-config.yml, using the format in the testing guide. Prefer certificate verification; disable it only when explicitly intended for the lab.

items.title: Plan cleanup and restoration
items.text:
Workspace discard is an additional safeguard for uncommitted database changes. It does not reverse every API operation or an installation onto a FortiGate. Live tests register owned resources and attempt compensating cleanup; interrupted execution or cleanup failures can still leave changes behind.

Review the selected tests, run live sessions serially, and inspect cleanup failures. Installation tests require explicit baseline authorization and --run-baseline-tests. Restore the baseline only through the authorized procedure.

items.title: Test trees and PyCharm
items.text:
tests/
  unit/                  # Offline tests, grouped by module
    client/
    common/
    dynamic/
    firewall/
    lab_helpers/         # Cleanup infrastructure tested with mocks
    policy/
    system/
    fixtures/            # Frozen schema references
  transport/             # Offline loopback HTTP checks
  lab/                   # Live FMG scenarios
    sync/
      objects/
    async/
      objects/
    fixtures.py          # Function-scoped live connections
    resources.py         # Ownership and compensating cleanup

Default pytest discovery selects tests/unit and tests/transport. Live connection fixtures and credential loading are confined to tests/lab; offline tests do not load the lab configuration. All paths below are relative to the repository root.

uv sync --locked
uv run pytest tests/unit tests/transport
uv run pytest tests/unit/firewall
uv run pytest tests/unit/firewall/test_service_ports.py
uv run invoke test
uv run invoke test --module unit

PyCharm loads shared configurations from .run/. The Offline tests, Unit test files, and Firewall modules folders provide combined, module-level, per-file, and per-firewall-family runs. The Lab tests, Lab tests - sync, and Lab tests - async folders target only the live tree. Configurations use the module's interpreter (the project's .venv) and the repository root as the working directory. Lab configurations pass --lab_config private/lab-config.yml. Regular lab configurations omit the baseline option; Lab - all - with baseline explicitly enables --run-baseline-tests for an authorized baseline/installation run. Configuration checks use targets and display names, so filenames can be renamed. Reopen the project if the IDE has not yet refreshed the shared configuration list.

The previous .idea state and test files were backed up locally under private/pycharm-tests-backup-* before replacement. This backup is gitignored and may contain local IDE settings. With PyCharm closed, restore its .idea/workspace.xml to recover the old local run entries, and move the generated .run directory aside if you want to hide the new shared entries. Non-test run configurations were preserved.

After reviewing and authorizing the selected lab operations, run a live module or branch serially:

uv run pytest tests/lab/sync/objects/test_firewall_extended.py --lab_config private/lab-config.yml -ra
uv run invoke lab-test --module async

invoke lab-test --baseline additionally enables installation scenarios and requires the authorized baseline/restore procedure. invoke test runs offline checks only.

items.title: Testing config file
items.text:
Store lab configuration and credentials in the gitignored private/ directory. Keep private/lab-config.yml local and never include credentials in diagnostics or commits. Prefer certificate verification; set verify: false only when explicitly intended for the lab.

Example of lab-config.yml file:

---
fmg:
  base_url: https://myfmg.co.com/
  verify: true
  username: admin
  password: "<lab-password>"
  adom: root

items.title: Offline regression tests
items.text: Run uv run pytest tests/unit (or pytest tests/unit in an activated environment) to check shared sync and async behavior without a lab configuration or network access. These tests mock the transport and exercise the public client methods.

items.title: Python 3.14+ compatibility
items.text:
Python 3.14 introduced deferred annotation evaluation. Models with fields named after builtins must qualify those builtins in annotations, including annotations that appear before the field. For example, Address.list requires builtins.list[str] in associated_interface's annotation; bare list[str] can resolve to the field's None default and fail during import.

tests/unit/common/test_model_annotations.py discovers all package models, including nested models, and rebuilds validation and serialization schemas. Run it on each supported Python version to catch annotation resolution errors across model fields and recursive references.

items.title: Async test event loops
items.text: The development dependencies require pytest-asyncio 0.24 or newer. Pytest uses auto mode and defaults async fixtures to function-scoped event loops. AsyncTestCase uses function-scoped connections and resources, so setup, requests, cleanup, and logout run on the same loop. Only the connection explicitly requested by a test is opened.

items.title: Live test isolation and cleanup
items.text:
For high-level model responses, response[value, "field"] raises AttributeError if the model has no such attribute. A valid field with no matching value returns None, including an unset optional field. Sync and async responses share this behavior. Raw dictionary lookups retain their existing permissive behavior; they do not have a model schema for validating field names.

GET treats an absent object as a successful empty lookup. Low-level clients return success=True and data=[{"data": [], "status": {"code": 0}}], consistently with the normal result-list shape. This replaces the previous inconsistent success=False and bare dictionary for missing objects. High-level callers receive an empty object list and .first() returns None. Request success and object presence are separate checks; permission, transport, and malformed-response errors remain errors and must never be interpreted as absence.

Each live test owns its setup and cleanup. Low-level address CRUD steps form one lifecycle test rather than depending on earlier test methods. Request lab (high-level) or base_lab (low-level) to register resources before writing them. lab.object(Model, "label", **fields) creates a bound model with a per-test name and reserves its delete URL; it does not add the object. Async tests await this method. Labels are at most six alphanumeric characters. For raw requests, call reserve(url) before the write. Existing resources are rejected, never adopted or deleted. Legacy batch scenarios retain fixed names but check absence before use.

Teardown checks and deletes owned resources in reverse registration order, verifies absence, and attempts remaining cleanup even if one operation fails. Register parents before children (addresses before groups, interfaces before zones). Cleanup runs before logout and also after failed assertions or partially successful writes. Failures identify the remaining resource URLs without printing raw transport exceptions. lab.wait(response) tracks unfinished tasks; device deletion uses its command API and waits for completion. Workspace discard is an additional safeguard.

The audit found these previous leak paths:

Tests Previous risk Organization now Low-level address CRUD Ordered methods and a final cleanup test One lifecycle with failure-path teardown Firewall mapping, groups, services Server mapping, third member, service left behind Owned resource journal Normalized interfaces Replaced an existing TEST object Unique owned interface VLAN, zone, administrator Objects left behind; first device selected Explicit FG01 and reverse cleanup Device and ADOM lifecycle Fixed-name collision, existing ADOM deletion, unfinished jobs Unique names and task-aware cleanup Batch operations Partial writes bypassed final deletes Reservation before the first write Authentication fault injection Lost real session token or URL prevented logout Mocked unit coverage; live login smoke only Installation Changed description and installed device configuration No description mutation; baseline-only test

The async directory now uses actual async clients for system, policy, dynamic interface, and installation checks. Duplicate scenarios were consolidated; a lower collected test count does not mean the CRUD steps were removed.

Install tests carry requires_baseline and are skipped unless --run-baseline-tests is supplied with an explicitly authorized baseline and restore procedure. They can install unrelated pending settings, so object cleanup cannot make them atomic. Restore the authorized snapshot after these tests; the suite does not automate Hyper-V restoration.

Cleanup is compensating work, not a database transaction. A killed process, unreachable device, or a task completing after a timeout can still leave state behind. Inspect reported resources and restore the authorized baseline when needed. Do not rerun failed writes blindly. The new cleanup paths require live firmware verification before claiming that the entire lab is restored after every failure.

items.title: Additional firewall lab scenarios
items.text:
The following files contain 16 independent live scenarios (eight synchronous and eight asynchronous) for the schema-backed firewall objects:

  • tests/lab/sync/objects/test_firewall_extended.py
  • tests/lab/async/objects/test_async_firewall_extended.py
Objects Coverage ProxyAddress, VIP, IPPool Add, read, update, refresh, set, delete, verify absence ProxyAddressGroup Owned members, add/read, clone, membership update/set, delete IPPoolGroup Owned CGN pools, add/read, exclusive-membership clone rejection, update/set, delete VIP, IPPool dynamic mappings Add scoped override, read typed mapping, change override, remove mapping InternetService Bounded read of one catalog record followed by a high-level ID-filtered lookup

These tests refuse an ADOM other than test. Mapping scenarios require the existing FG01 device, its root VDOM, and port1 for the VIP interface override. They do not install configuration, create devices/ADOMs, change workspace mode, or modify pre-existing objects. Every created or cloned object is reserved with lab before its write. Member resources are registered before groups, so teardown removes references before their parents. Cleanup also runs after a failed assertion or partial write. The catalog test makes no writes and skips explicitly if the Internet Service Database is empty.

The implementation reference is FMG 7.6.7 with FortiOS 7.4 ADOM objects. The lab must support the selected endpoints and fields; older firmware or a missing feature may fail a scenario. These new scenarios were exercised on FMG 7.4.6 build 2588. IP pool groups require CGN resource-allocation pools and reject cloning a populated group because pools cannot belong to two groups. The tests check that specific rejection and verify that no clone was created. FMG 7.6.7 itself remains unverified. After authorizing their object writes, run the scenarios serially:

uv run pytest tests/lab/sync/objects/test_firewall_extended.py tests/lab/async/objects/test_async_firewall_extended.py --lab_config private/lab-config.yml -ra

For collection without a lab connection, add --collect-only and use a nonexistent config path.

The verified FMG 7.4.6 run completed with 14 passed and 2 skipped: the catalog count was zero, so both InternetService lookups skipped. Cleanup verification found no remaining journaled objects, the five object-table name inventories matched their pre-run baseline, and ADOM test had no workspace lock records. No configuration was installed.

items.title: Local transport checks
items.text: Run uv run pytest tests/transport to verify native HTTP timeouts against a temporary loopback-only TCP peer. These tests need permission to create local sockets and do not connect to a FortiManager device.

items.title: Workspace verification notes
items.text:
These recorded checks describe workspace discovery and Global Database locking on FMG 7.4.6. They are historical verification evidence, not a verification run for this documentation change.

Workspace discovery and locking were verified on FMG 7.4.6 build 2588 by temporarily changing global mode and the test ADOM's workspace setting through all 12 combinations, reading both levels, and probing Global Database locks. All settings were restored, acquired locks released, and sessions logged out; no policy/object changes, configuration installs, or workspace commits were performed.

Global workspace-mode Requested ADOM workspace_mode Returned ADOM workspace_mode Global lock result disabled 0, 1, or 2 0 -9 (unavailable) normal 0, 1, or 2 1 0 (success) workflow 0, 1, or 2 2 0 (success) per-adom 0, 1, or 2 Requested value -9 (unavailable)

The ADOM metadata reports the effective mode, including global overrides. A lock-info record's db_mode is not a substitute: it reported 1 for a locked ADOM even under global workflow. Neither /dvmdb/adom/global nor /dvmdb/adom/Global returned metadata (status -3), and the ADOM inventory contained no Global Database entry. GET /dvmdb/global/workspace/lockinfo returned -9 under disabled and per-adom, and succeeded under normal and workflow. The explicit Global Database rule comes from these controlled checks, not from treating arbitrary failed metadata reads as disabled workspace. Failed ordinary ADOM discovery still raises FMGLockException. Other firmware versions have not been verified against a device. See Fortinet's workspace configuration guide.

items.title: FMGSettings
items.text:
Bases: BaseSettings

Connection and resilience settings for FortiManager clients.

Attributes:

Name Type Description base_url Annotated[HttpUrl, Field(description='Base URL to access FMG (e.g.: https://myfmg/jsonrpc)')]

FortiManager HTTPS URL; /jsonrpc is appended if absent.

username Annotated[str, Field(description='User to authenticate')]

Account with JSON-RPC API access.

password Annotated[SecretStr, Field(description='Password for authentication')]

Authentication password, stored as a Pydantic SecretStr.

adom Annotated[str, Field(description='ADOM to use for this connection')]

Selected ADOM or "global" for the Global Database. Defaults to "global".

verify Annotated[bool, Field(description='Verify SSL certificate (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE can set accepted CA cert)')]

Verify TLS certificates. Defaults to True. REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE applies to the sync transport.

timeout Annotated[float, Field(gt=0, allow_inf_nan=False, description='Connect/read timeout in seconds')]

Connect/read inactivity timeout per transport attempt, in seconds.

retry_attempts Annotated[int, Field(ge=1, description='Total transport attempts for read requests')]

Maximum transport attempts for read requests, including the initial call.

retry_delay Annotated[float, Field(ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False, description='Initial retry delay in seconds')]

Initial retry delay in seconds.

retry_backoff Annotated[float, Field(ge=1, allow_inf_nan=False, description='Retry delay multiplier')]

Retry delay multiplier.

retry_max_delay Annotated[float, Field(ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False, description='Maximum retry delay in seconds')]

Maximum retry delay in seconds.

retry_jitter bool

Randomize retry delays.

raise_on_error Annotated[bool, Field(description='Raise exception on error')]

Raise library exceptions for decorated API operations instead of failed responses.

discard_on_close Annotated[bool, Field(description='Discard changes after connection close (workspace mode)')]

Skip workspace commits during close. Defaults to False.

discard_on_error Annotated[bool, Field(description='Discard changes when exception occurs (workspace mode)')]

Skip workspace commits when an exception exits the context. Defaults to True.

Notes

Discard settings do not reverse configuration installations or every device operation.

check and fix base_url

Source code in pyfortinet/settings.py

General API URL assembly

Source code in pyfortinet/fmg_api/__init__.py 
def get_url(self, method: Literal["get", "add", "set", "update", "delete", "clone", "exec"] = "get") -> str:
    """General API URL assembly

    To be overridden by more complex API URLs in different classes
    """
    variables = re.findall(r"{(.*?)}", self._url)
    if not self.fmg_scope:
        if "scope" in variables:
            raise FMGMissingScopeException(f"Missing scope for {self}")
    url = self._url
    for field in variables:
        if field == "scope":
            url = url.replace(f"{{{field}}}", self.fmg_scope)
        else:
            if hasattr(self, field) and getattr(self, field) is not None:
                url = url.replace(f"{{{field}}}", str(getattr(self, field)))
            elif (
                method in ("get", "set", "update", "delete", "clone")
                and field in self.master_keys
                and getattr(self, self.master_keys[field], None) is not None
            ):  # certain methods require master key (like policyid)
                url = url.replace(f"{{{field}}}", str(getattr(self, self.master_keys[field])))
            # delete field from URL if no data found (can lead to errors)
            elif method in ("get", "add", "set", "update") and url.endswith(f"{{{field}}}"):
                url = url.replace(f"/{{{field}}}", "")
            else:
                raise FMGInvalidURL(f"Missing field '{field}' for ({self._url})")
    return url

def model_dump_for_filter(self) -> dict:
    """Modified pydantic model dump for FMG API

    This method will include otherwise excluded fields to use them in FMG.get method filtering.
    Special attention is made for URL fields which must not be included in the filters as they are not part of the
    payload.
    """
    # get the normal dump first
    dump = self.model_dump(by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    # include excluded not-none fields
    excluded_fields = {}
    for field_name, field_model in type(self).model_fields.items():
        # check only excluded vars which are not None and are not URL attributes (cannot be used as filter)
        if field_model.exclude and getattr(self, field_name) is not None and f"{{{field_name}}}" not in self._url:
            excluded_fields[field_model.serialization_alias or field_name] = getattr(self, field_name)

    dump.update(excluded_fields)
    return dump

def prepare_batch(request, *, allow_objects=False):
    """Normalize a write request and reject empty or mixed batches."""
    requests = request if isinstance(request, list) else [request]
    if not requests:
        raise FMGWrongRequestException("Request list must not be empty")
    if isinstance(requests[0], dict):
        expected_type = dict
    elif allow_objects and isinstance(requests[0], FMGObject):
        expected_type = FMGObject
    else:
        raise FMGWrongRequestException(f"Wrong type of request received: {request}")
    if not all(isinstance(item, expected_type) for item in requests):
        raise FMGWrongRequestException("Batch requests must all be dictionaries or all be FMGObject instances")
    return requests

Source code in pyfortinet/fmg_api/_requests.py 
def prepare_get(request, adom, *, filters=None, scope=None, fields=None, loadsub=True, options=None):  # noqa: PLR0913
    """Build high-level GET parameters and retain the effective object scope."""
    if isinstance(filters, str):
        filters = text_to_filter(filters)
    object_scope = scope or adom
    if isinstance(request, FMGObject):
        request.fmg_scope = request.fmg_scope or object_scope
        url = request.get_url()
        object_scope = getattr(request, "adom", None) or request.fmg_scope
        field_names = {
            definition.serialization_alias or name: name for name, definition in type(request).model_fields.items()
        }
        for field in request.model_dump_for_filter():
            value = getattr(request, field_names.get(field, field))
            condition = F(**{field: value})
            filters = filters & condition if filters else condition
    elif isclass(request) and issubclass(request, FMGObject):
        url = re.sub(r"/{(?!scope).*?}", "", request._url.default)
        if object_scope != "global" and not object_scope.startswith("adom/"):
            object_scope = f"adom/{object_scope}"
        url = url.replace("{scope}", object_scope)
    else:
        raise FMGWrongRequestException(f"Wrong type of request received: {request}")

    parameters = {"url": url, "loadsub": 1 if loadsub else 0}
    if filters:
        parameters["filter"] = filters.generate()
    if fields is not None:
        parameters["fields"] = fields
    if options:
        parameters["option"] = options
    return parameters, object_scope

def _retry_config(
    settings: FMGSettings,
    request: dict[str, Any],
    retry_on: tuple[type[Exception], ...],
    ignore_on: tuple[type[Exception], ...],
) -> RetryConfig:

    return RetryConfig(

        delay=settings.retry_delay,
        backoff_factor=settings.retry_backoff,
        max_delay=settings.retry_max_delay,
        jitter=settings.retry_jitter,
        retry_on=(_TransientHTTPError, *retry_on),
        ignore_on=ignore_on,
    )

async def async_request_json(
    session: "aiohttp.ClientSession", settings: FMGSettings, request: dict[str, Any], *, timeout: Optional[float] = None
) -> Any:
    """Send and decode an async request with the same native I/O timeout policy."""
    import aiohttp  # noqa: PLC0415 - optional async dependency

    retry = _retry_config(
        settings, request, (aiohttp.ClientConnectionError, asyncio.TimeoutError), (aiohttp.ClientSSLError,)
    )
    seconds = timeout_seconds(settings.timeout if timeout is None else timeout)
    timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=None, connect=seconds, sock_connect=seconds, sock_read=seconds)

    @resilient(retry=retry)
    async def attempt():
        response = await session.post(str(settings.base_url), json=request, ssl=settings.verify, timeout=timeout)
        try:
            _check_status(response.status)
            try:
                return await response.json()
            except (ValueError, aiohttp.ContentTypeError) as err:
                raise FMGUnhandledException("Invalid JSON-RPC response: expected JSON") from err
        finally:
            response.release()

    return await attempt()

def request_json(session: requests.Session, settings: FMGSettings, request: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    """Send and decode a sync request, releasing each response before any retry."""
    retry = _retry_config(
        settings, request, (requests.ConnectionError, requests.Timeout), (requests.exceptions.SSLError,)
    )
    seconds = timeout_seconds(settings.timeout)

    @resilient(retry=retry)
    def attempt():
        response = session.post(str(settings.base_url), json=request, verify=settings.verify, timeout=seconds)
        try:
            _check_status(response.status_code)
            try:
                return response.json()
            except ValueError as err:
                raise FMGUnhandledException("Invalid JSON-RPC response: expected JSON") from err
        finally:
            response.close()

    return attempt()

def timeout_seconds(value: float) -> float:
    """Validate temporary timeout overrides as well as configured values."""
    value = float(value)
    if not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0:
        raise ValueError("timeout must be a finite number greater than zero")
    return value

def login_token(payload):
    """Require a successful login result and a nonempty session token."""
    results = payload.get("result") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(results, list) or not results or not isinstance(results[0], dict):
        raise FMGTokenException("Login failed, malformed authentication response")
    status = results[0].get("status")
    if not isinstance(status, dict) or "code" not in status:
        raise FMGTokenException("Login failed, malformed authentication response")
    if status["code"] != 0:
        message = status.get("message")
        if isinstance(message, str) and "No permission for resource" in message:
            raise FMGUnhandledException("No permission for resource, probably user does not have API access!")
        raise FMGTokenException("Login failed, wrong credentials!")
    token = payload.get("session")
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
        raise FMGTokenException("Login failed, missing or invalid session token")
    return SecretStr(token)

def rpc_result(payload):
    """Validate result envelopes before interpreting API status codes."""
    results = payload.get("result") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(results, list) or not results:
        raise FMGUnhandledException("Malformed JSON-RPC response: expected a nonempty result list")
    for result in results:
        status = result.get("status") if isinstance(result, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(status, dict) or not isinstance(status.get("code"), int):
            raise FMGUnhandledException("Malformed JSON-RPC response: missing or invalid status code")
        if status["code"] != 0:
            error = get_fmg_error(error_code=status["code"])
            if error is not None and not isinstance(error, str):
                raise error(status)
            raise FMGUnhandledException(status)
    return results[0] if len(results) == 1 else results

def workspace_mode(response, field="workspace-mode"):
    """Read a known workspace mode from a successful discovery reply."""
    if not response.success or not isinstance(response.data, list) or not response.data:
        raise FMGLockException("Unable to determine workspace mode")
    result = response.data[0]
    data = result.get("data") if isinstance(result, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise FMGLockException("Unable to determine workspace mode")
    mode = data.get(field)
    modes = {0: "disabled", 1: "normal", 2: "workflow", 3: "per-adom"}
    if isinstance(mode, str) and mode.isdigit():
        mode = int(mode)
    if isinstance(mode, int):
        mode = modes.get(mode)
    if mode not in modes.values():
        raise FMGLockException("Unable to determine workspace mode")
    return mode

def task_from_response(response):
    """Decode a task from a successful low-level GET result."""
    if not response.success:
        return None
    result = response.first()
    if result is None:
        return None
    data = result.get("data")

def task_id_from_response(response):
    """Read either task identifier spelling returned by FortiManager."""
    if isinstance(response, int):
        return response
    if not response.success:
        return None
    data = response.data
    if isinstance(data, list):
        data = data[0] if data else {}
    data = data.get("data") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return None
    task_id = data.get("taskid")
    return task_id if task_id is not None else data.get("task")

async def clone(self, request: REQUEST_ARG, *, create_task: bool = False, **new: str) -> AsyncFMGResponse:
    """Clone one configuration object using new identity values.

    Args:
        request: Source model or raw clone request dictionary.
        create_task: Request a background task. Keep the connection open until it finishes.
        **new: New identity fields, usually name, matching the model's master keys.

    Returns:
        AsyncFMGResponse: Clone operation status, with task metadata when provided by FortiManager.

    Examples:
        Inside an open connection, clone an existing address to an unused name:

        ```python
        from pyfortinet.fmg_api.firewall import Address

        response = await fmg.clone(Address(name="example-server"), name="example-server-copy")
        ```
    """
    response = AsyncFMGResponse(fmg=self)
    if isinstance(request, dict):  # JSON input, low-level operation
        return await super().clone(request, create_task=create_task)
    elif isinstance(request, FMGObject):  # high-level operation
        if not request.master_keys:
            raise FMGMissingMasterKeyException(f"Need to specify a master key for {request}")
        # master_key = first(request.master_keys.values())  # assume one master_key, like `name`
        # master_value = getattr(request, master_key)
        request.fmg_scope = request.fmg_scope or self._settings.adom
        return await super().clone(
            {
                "url": request.get_url(method="clone"),
                "data": new,
            },
            create_task=create_task,
        )
    else:
        response.data = {"error": f"Wrong type of request received: {request}"}
        response.status = 400
        logger.error(response.data["error"])
        if self._raise_on_error:
            raise FMGWrongRequestException(request)
        return response

async def exec(self, request: Union[dict[str, Any], FMGExecObject]) -> AsyncFMGResponse:

@error_handling
@auth_required
async def get(
    self,
    request: Union[dict[str, Any], FMGObject, Type[FMGObject]],
    filters: Union[str, FILTER_TYPE] = None,
    scope: Optional[str] = None,
    fields: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    loadsub: bool = True,
    options: Optional[List[GetOption]] = None,
    **kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, str]],
) -> AsyncFMGResponse:
    """Read objects from FortiManager.

    Args:
        request: Model class for a collection, initialized model for selection, or raw request dictionary.
        filters: Filter expression as text or composed with F.
        scope: Request scope; an explicit model scope takes precedence.
        fields: API field names to request, or None for all fields.
        loadsub: Request nested tables.
        options: Additional API GET options.

    Returns:
        AsyncFMGResponse: High-level data contains bound models. A successful empty lookup
        has an empty data list and first() returns None. Dictionary requests retain raw results.

    Examples:
        Use configured connection settings and handle an empty lookup:

        ```python
        from pyfortinet import AsyncFMG
        from pyfortinet.fmg_api.common import F
        from pyfortinet.fmg_api.firewall import Address

        async with AsyncFMG(**config) as fmg:
            response = await fmg.get(Address, F(name__like="server%"))
            for address in response.data:
                print(address.name, address.subnet)
            server = (await fmg.get(Address(name="server1"))).first()
            if server is not None:
                print(server.name)
        ```
    """
    # Call base function for base arguments
    if isinstance(request, dict):
        return await super().get(request)
    # High level arguments
    result = AsyncFMGResponse(fmg=self)
    api_request, object_scope = prepare_get(
        request, self.adom, filters=filters, scope=scope, fields=fields, loadsub=loadsub, options=options
    )

    body = {
        "method": "get",
        "params": [api_request],
        "verbose": 1,
        "session": self._token.get_secret_value(),
        "id": self._id,
    }

    try:
        api_result = await self._post(request=body)
    except FMGObjectNotExistException:
        api_result = {"data": []}

    # construct object list
    objects = []
    obj_class = type(request) if isinstance(request, FMGObject) else request
    url_fields = response_url_fields(request)
    values = api_result.get("data")
    if values is None:
        values = []
    elif not isinstance(values, list):
        values = [values]
    for value in values:
        objects.append(obj_class(**{**url_fields, **value}, fmg_scope=object_scope, fmg=self))
    result.data = objects
    result.success = True
    return result

async def get_adom_list(self, filters: FILTER_TYPE = None) -> Optional[List[str]]:
    """Gather adoms from FMG

    Args:
        filters: filter as list or F object

    Returns:
        list of adom strings or None in case of error
    """
    request = {"url": "/dvmdb/adom", "fields": ["name"]}
    if filters:
        request["filter"] = self._get_filter_list(filters)

    response: AsyncFMGResponse = await self.get(request)
    if response.success:
        return [adom.get("name") for adom in response.data[0].get("data")]
    return None

def get_obj(self, obj: Union[Type[FMGObject], Type[FMGExecObject], AnyFMGObject], **kwargs: Any) -> AnyFMGObject:
    """Construct or bind a local model to this client without an API request.

    Args:
        obj: FMGObject or FMGExecObject class, or an existing instance.
        **kwargs: Initialization fields when obj is a class; ignored for existing instances.

    Returns:
        AnyFMGObject: A new instance for a class argument, or the same bound instance for an object argument.

    Examples:
        This method is synchronous for both clients. Creating the model does not create the remote object:

        ```python
        from pyfortinet.fmg_api.firewall import Address

        address = fmg.get_obj(Address, name="example-server", subnet="192.0.2.10/32")
        ```
    """
    if isinstance(obj, (FMGObject, FMGExecObject)):
        obj._fmg = self
        return obj
    elif isclass(obj) and issubclass(obj, (FMGObject, FMGExecObject)):
        return obj(fmg=self, **kwargs)

    raise TypeError(f"Argument {obj} is not an FMGObject or FMGExecObject type")

Source code in pyfortinet/fmg_api/async_fmg.py 
async def refresh(self, obj: FMGObject) -> FMGObject:
    """Re-load data from FMG"""
    if not obj.master_keys:
        raise FMGMissingMasterKeyException
    # Use master key fields only to identify this object, filters are not appropriate as there might be URL
    # fields amongst master keys
    new = await self.get(prepare_refresh(obj))
    if not new.success:
        raise FMGWrongRequestException("Cannot refresh object because the lookup failed")
    if len(new.data) != 1:
        raise FMGWrongRequestException(
            f"{obj} need to load from FMG first in order to call .refresh()!",
        )
    new = new.first()
    if new:
        # overwrite our object fields with data from FMG
        for att, definition in type(obj).model_fields.items():
            if not definition.exclude:  # excluded fields should not be overwritten (e.g. URL fields)
                setattr(obj, att, getattr(new, att))
    return obj

def __init__(self, settings: Optional[FMGSettings] = None, **kwargs):
    """Initializes FMGBase

    Args:
        settings (Settings): FortiManager settings

    Keyword Args:
        base_url (str): Base URL to access FMG (e.g.: https://myfmg)
        username (str): User to authenticate
        password (str): Password for authentication
        adom (str): ADOM to use for this connection
        verify (bool): Verify SSL certificate (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE can set accepted CA cert)
        timeout (float): Connect/read inactivity timeout per transport attempt, in seconds
        raise_on_error (bool): Raise exception on error
        discard_on_close (bool): Discard changes after connection close (workspace mode)
        discard_on_error (bool): Discard changes when exception occurs (workspace mode)
    """
    try:
        import aiohttp
    except ModuleNotFoundError:

close connection

Source code in pyfortinet/fmg_api/async_fmgbase.py 
async def close(self, discard_changes: bool = False):
    """close connection"""
    session = self._session
    workspace_error = None
    try:
        if session is None or self._token is None:
            return
        request = {
            "id": self._id,
            "method": "exec",
            "params": [{"url": "/sys/logout"}],
            "session": self._token.get_secret_value(),
        }
        if self.lock.locked_adoms or self.lock.uses_workspace:
            if not (self.discard_on_close or discard_changes):
                try:
                    responses = await self.lock.commit_changes()
                    if any(not response.success for response in responses):
                        raise FMGLockException("Failed to commit workspace changes")
                except FMGException as err:
                    workspace_error = err
                    logger.exception("Failed to commit workspace changes")
            try:
                await self.lock.unlock_adoms()
            except FMGException as err:
                workspace_error = workspace_error or err
                logger.exception("Failed to unlock workspaces")
        payload = await async_request_json(session, self._settings, request, timeout=self._timeout_override.get())
        status = payload.get("result", [{}])[0].get("status", {})
        if status.get("code") != 0:
            logger.warning("Logout failed!")
    except aiohttp.ClientConnectionError:
        logger.warning("Logout failed!")
    except (FMGException, aiohttp.ClientError, asyncio.TimeoutError):
        if workspace_error is None:
            raise
        logger.exception("Logout failed after workspace cleanup failed")
    finally:
        try:
            if session is not None:
                await session.close()
        finally:
            self._session = None
            self._token = None
            self.lock.locked_adoms.clear()
            self.lock._uses_workspace = None
            self.lock._uses_adoms = None
        logger.debug("Closed session")
    if workspace_error is not None:
        raise workspace_error

async def get(self, request: dict[str, Any]) -> AsyncFMGResponse:  # noqa: PLR0912 - Too many branches
    """Get info from FMG

    This method currently does not support multiple requests in one call!

    Args:
        request: Get operation's param structure

    Examples:
        ```pycon

        >>> import asyncio
        >>> address_request = {
        ...    "url": "/pm/config/global/obj/firewall/address",
        ...    "filter": [ ["name", "==", "test-address"] ],
        ...    "fields": [ "name", "subnet" ]
        ... }

        ...     async with AsyncFMGBase(**settings) as fmg:
        ...         return await fmg.get(address_request)
        >>> asyncio.run(get_address())
        ```

    Returns:
        (AsyncFMGResponse): response object with data
    """
    body = {
        "method": "get",
        "params": [request],
        "verbose": 1,  # get string values instead of numeric
        "session": self._token.get_secret_value(),
        "id": self._id,
    }
    result = AsyncFMGResponse(fmg=self)
    try:
        api_result = await self._post(request=body)
    except FMGObjectNotExistException:
        # handling when specific requested object doesn't exist
        # we don't error out, but give an empty list
        result.data = [{"data": [], "status": {"code": 0}}]
        result.success = True
        return result

    # handling empty result list
    if not api_result:
        result.data = [{"data": [], "status": {"code": 0}}]
        result.success = True
        return result

    # processing result list
    result.data = api_result if isinstance(api_result, list) else [api_result]
    result.success = True
    # result.status = api_result.get("status", {}).get("code", 400)

    return result

@asynccontextmanager
async def lock_adom(self, adom: Optional[str] = None, keep_locked: bool = False):
    """Locks specified ADOM explicitly

    The usual error based locking not always work. For example FMG replies authentication error while running
    a job to create new Device in device database. This makes error handling unusable and therefore this
    context manager can be used to lock ADOM for the job run duration.

    If adom was already locked, this function won't lock it again and won't unlock it either.

    Args:
        adom: ADOM to be locked as string. If not specified, currently used ADOM will be used.
        keep_locked: If True, the lock is not released after operation. (default: False)

    Yields:
        (str): adom name (not used normally)
    """
    if not adom:
        adom = self.adom
    if not adom:
        raise ValueError("ADOM must be specified!")
    await self.lock.check_mode(adom)
    did_lock = False
    if self.lock.uses_workspace and adom not in self.lock.locked_adoms:
        await self.lock.lock_adoms(adom)
        did_lock = True
    try:
        yield adom
    finally:
        if did_lock and not keep_locked:
            await self.lock.unlock_adoms(adom)

async def open(self) -> "AsyncFMGBase":
    """open connection"""
    if self._session is not None and self._token is not None:
        return self
    logger.debug("Initializing connection to %s with id: %s", self._settings.base_url, self._id)
    self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession()
    try:
        self._token = await self._get_token()
    except BaseException:
        session, self._session = self._session, None
        self._token = None
        await session.close()
        raise
    return self

    timeout: int = 60,
    loop_interval: int = 2,
) -> Union[str, None]:
    """Poll a FortiManager task until it reaches a terminal state.

    Args:

        Inside an open connection, use a task ID returned by an earlier execution request:

        ```python
        state = await fmg.wait_for_task(task_id, callback=lambda percent, log: print(percent, log))
        ```
    """
    task_id = task_id_from_response(task_res)
    if task_id is None:
        return
    start_time = time.monotonic()
    while True:
        try:
            response = await self.get({"url": Task._url.default, "filter": ["id", "==", task_id]})
            task: Task = task_from_response(response)
        except aiohttp.ClientConnectionError:
            await asyncio.sleep(loop_interval)
            if time.monotonic() - start_time > timeout:
                raise TimeoutError(f"Timed out waiting {timeout} seconds for the task {task_id}!") from None
            continue
        if not task:
            return
        if time.monotonic() - start_time > timeout:
            raise TimeoutError(f"Timed out waiting {timeout} seconds for the task {task_id}!")
        if callable(callback):
            callback_result = callback(task.percent, task.line[-1].detail if task.line else "")
            if isawaitable(callback_result):
                await callback_result
        # exit on the following states
        if task.state in TERMINAL_TASK_STATES:
            return task.state
        await asyncio.sleep(loop_interval)

async def check_mode(self, adom: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    """Discover the effective workspace mode for the requested or selected ADOM."""
    self._uses_workspace = None
    result = await self._fmg.get({"url": "/cli/global/system/global", "fields": ["workspace-mode"]})
    if workspace_mode(result) == "per-adom":
        adom = adom or self._fmg.adom or "root"
        if adom.lower() == "global":
            # FMG 7.4.6 exposes no global ADOM metadata and disables its workspace in per-ADOM mode.
            enabled = False
        else:
            result = await self._fmg.get({"url": f"/dvmdb/adom/{adom}", "fields": ["workspace_mode"]})
            enabled = workspace_enabled(result, "workspace_mode")
    else:
        enabled = workspace_enabled(result)
    self._uses_workspace = enabled

async def commit_changes(self, adoms: Optional[list] = None, aux: bool = False) -> list[AsyncFMGResponse]:
    """Commit workspace changes in FortiManager's database.

    Args:
        adoms: ADOM names to commit. If omitted or empty, use the ADOMs locked by this client.
        aux: Use the policy/object database workspace commit route.

    Returns:
        list: Responses for the commit operations. This does not install configuration onto devices.
    """
    results = []
    if not adoms:
        adoms = self._locked_adoms
    for adom in adoms:
        if aux:
            url = f"/pm/config/adom/{adom}/workspace/commit"
        elif adom.lower() == "global":
            url = "/dvmdb/global/workspace/commit/"
        else:
            url = f"/dvmdb/adom/{adom}/workspace/commit"
        results.append(await self._fmg.exec({"url": url}))
    return results

async def lock_adoms(self, *adoms: str) -> AsyncFMGResponse:
    """Lock adom list

    If no adom specified, global workspace will be locked

    Args:
        *adoms (str): list of adom names

    Returns:
        Response object
    """
    result = AsyncFMGResponse(fmg=self._fmg, data=[], success=True)
    if not adoms:
        adoms = ["root"]
    for adom in adoms:
        url = "/dvmdb/global/workspace/lock/" if adom.lower() == "global" else f"/dvmdb/adom/{adom}/workspace/lock/"
        operation = await self._fmg.exec(request={"url": url})
        result.data.append({adom: operation})
        if not operation.success:
            raise FMGLockException(operation.data)
        self._locked_adoms.add(adom)
    return result

async def unlock_adoms(self, *adoms) -> AsyncFMGResponse:
    """unlock ADOMs"""
    result = AsyncFMGResponse(fmg=self._fmg, data=[], success=True)
    if not adoms:
        adoms = copy(self._locked_adoms)
    failed_adoms = set()
    for adom in adoms:
        if adom.lower() == "global":
            url = "/dvmdb/global/workspace/unlock/"
        else:
            url = f"/dvmdb/adom/{adom}/workspace/unlock/"
        operation = await self._fmg.exec(request={"url": url})
        result.data.append({adom: operation})
        if operation.success:
            self._locked_adoms.discard(adom)
        else:
            failed_adoms.add(adom)

    if failed_adoms:
        raise FMGException(f"Failed to unlock ADOMs: {failed_adoms}")
    return result

def auth_required(func: Callable) -> Callable:
    """Decorator to provide authentication for the method

    Args:
        func: function to handle authentication errors

    Returns:
        (Callable): function with authentication handling enabled
    """

    @functools.wraps(func)
    async def auth_decorated(self: Union[dict, "AsyncFMGBase"] = None, *args, **kwargs):
        """method which needs authentication"""
        if not self._token:
            raise FMGTokenException("No token was obtained. Open connection first!")
        try:
            return await func(self, *args, **kwargs)
        except FMGAuthenticationException as err:
            try:  # try again after refreshing token
                self._token = await self._get_token()  # pylint: disable=protected-access  # decorator of methods
                return await func(self, *args, **kwargs)
            except FMGException as err2:
                raise err2 from err

    return auth_decorated

def lock(func: Callable) -> Callable:
    """Decorator to provide ADOM locking if needed

    Args:
        func: function to handle errors complaining about no locking

    Returns:
        (Callable): function with lock handling enabled
    """

    @functools.wraps(func)
    async def lock_decorated(self: "AsyncFMGBase" = None, *args, **kwargs):
        """method which needs locking"""
        try:
            return await func(self, *args, **kwargs)
        except (FMGLockNeededException, FMGAuthenticationException) as err:
            try:  # try again after locking
                if not args:  # in case we got kwargs request
                    args = [kwargs.get("request")]
                    del kwargs["request"]
                # ensure args[0] is a list of request dict or obj to support multiple request in one API call
                if isinstance(args[0], list):
                    args_to_check = args[0]
                else:
                    args_to_check = [args[0]]
                for arg in args_to_check:
                    if isinstance(arg, dict):
                        url = arg.get("url")
                        adom_match = re.search(r"^(?:/\w+){,3}/(?P<adom>global\b|(?<=adom/)[\w-]+)/?", url)
                        if adom_match:
                            adom = adom_match.group("adom")
                        elif self.adom:
                            adom = self.adom
                        else:
                            raise FMGException(f"No ADOM found to lock in url '{url}'") from err
                    elif isinstance(arg, FMGObject):
                        adom = arg.fmg_scope
                    else:
                        raise ValueError(f"Unknown request: {arg}")
                    if adom not in self.lock.locked_adoms:
                        await self.lock(adom)
                    # else:  # ADOM already locked, do not try to lock it again
                    #     raise
                return await func(self, *args, **kwargs)
            except FMGException as err2:
                raise err2 from err

    return lock_decorated

def __init__(self, *, _sep="_", **kwargs):
    """Filter initialization"""
    if len(kwargs) > 1:
        raise ValueError(f"F only accepts one filter condition at a time!")
    for key, value in kwargs.items():
        if "__" in key:
            self.source, self.op = key.split("__")
            if self.op not in OP:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown operation: '{self.op}' !")
            self.op = OP[self.op]
        else:
            self.source = key
            self.op = "=="
        self.source = re.sub(r"(?!^)_", _sep, self.source)
        self.targets = value

def find_matching_parenthesis(input_string):
    """Helper function to find matching parenthesis

    Find the index of the closing parenthesis that matches the first opening parenthesis in the input string.

    Args:
        input_string (str): The string to be scanned for matching parentheses.

    Returns:
        (int): The index of the matching closing parenthesis if found, else returns None.
    """
    count = 1
    pos = 1
    while count > 0:
        open_paren_pos = input_string.find("(", pos)
        close_paren_pos = input_string.find(")", pos)
        if (open_paren_pos != -1 and open_paren_pos < close_paren_pos) or close_paren_pos == -1:
            pos = open_paren_pos
            count += 1
        else:
            pos = close_paren_pos
            count -= 1
        if pos == -1:
            return None
        pos += 1

    return pos - 1

items.text:
text_to_filter(text: str) -> FILTER_TYPE

Text to filter object

Format of the text follows the OP definition! This is a simple text to filter object converter. Parenthesis are supported. Simple field comparisons with and/or and , operators are supported. , means a simple or between same type fields. Field name can contain - and characters, refer to API docs for available field names.

structure::

fname fop fvalue OP fname fop fvalue OP ...
----------------    ----------------
    F token              F token

Examples:

simple F filter

>>> text_to_filter('name like host_%').generate()
['name', 'like', 'host_%']

inversing

>>> text_to_filter('~name like host_%').generate()
['!', 'name', 'like', 'host_%']

simple or function

>>> text_to_filter('name eq host_1, name eq host_2').generate()
[['name', '==', 'host_1'], ['name', '==', 'host_2']]

more complex filter

>>> text_to_filter('name eq host_1 and conf_status eq insync').generate()
[['name', '==', 'host_1'], '&&', ['conf_status', '==', 'insync']]

>>> assert text_to_filter("(name eq host_1 and (conf_status eq insync or conf_status eq modified))").generate()
[
    ["name", "==", "host_1"],
    "&&",
    [["conf_status", "==", "insync"], "||", ["conf_status", "==", "modified"]],
]

def text_to_filter(text: str) -> FILTER_TYPE:
    """Text to filter object

    Format of the text follows the ``OP`` definition!
    This is a simple text to filter object converter. Parenthesis are supported.
    Simple field comparisons with `and/or and ,` operators are supported. `,` means a simple `or` between same
    type fields.
    Field name can contain `-` and ` ` characters, refer to API docs for available field names.

    structure::

        fname fop fvalue OP fname fop fvalue OP ...
        ----------------    ----------------
            F token              F token

    Examples:
        simple F filter

        >>> text_to_filter('name like host_%').generate()
        ['name', 'like', 'host_%']

        inversing

        >>> text_to_filter('~name like host_%').generate()
        ['!', 'name', 'like', 'host_%']

        simple or function

        >>> text_to_filter('name eq host_1, name eq host_2').generate()
        [['name', '==', 'host_1'], ['name', '==', 'host_2']]

        more complex filter

        >>> text_to_filter('name eq host_1 and conf_status eq insync').generate()
        [['name', '==', 'host_1'], '&&', ['conf_status', '==', 'insync']]

        >>> assert text_to_filter("(name eq host_1 and (conf_status eq insync or conf_status eq modified))").generate()
        [
            ["name", "==", "host_1"],
            "&&",
            [["conf_status", "==", "insync"], "||", ["conf_status", "==", "modified"]],
        ]

    Args:
        text (str): Text to parse

    Returns:
        FILTER_TYPE: Filter object which can be used in FMG.get calls

     Raises:
         ValueError: text cannot be parsed
    """
    text = text.strip()
    if text.startswith("("):  # search the end of the ()
        end = find_matching_parenthesis(text)
        if end is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Couldn't parse '{text}'!")
        a = text_to_filter(text[1:end])
        remaining = text[end + 1 :]
        if remaining:  # operand should follow
            op = {"and": "&&", "or": "||", ",": ","}.get(remaining.split()[0])
            if op is None:
                raise ValueError(f"Couldn't parse '{text}'!")
            b = text_to_filter(" ".join(remaining.split()[1:]))
            # noinspection PyTypeChecker
            return ComplexFilter(a, op, b)  # treat parentheses as parts of ComplexFilter
        else:  # no operand found, end of input
            return a

    while text:
        # search F tokens
        f_match = re.match(
            rf"(?P<negate>~)?\s*(?P<fname>[\w -]+?)\s+(?P<fop>{'|'.join(OP.keys())})\s+(?P<fvalue>\S+)(?<![,|&])", text
        )
        if f_match:
            kwargs = {f"{f_match.group('fname')}__{f_match.group('fop')}": f_match.group("fvalue")}
            if f_match.group("negate"):
                f_token = ~F(**kwargs)
            else:
                f_token = F(**kwargs)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Couldn't parse '{text}'!")
        text = text[f_match.end() :].strip()
        if not text:
            return f_token
        # search list or complex filter ops
        op_match = re.match(rf"(?P<op>and|or|,)\s+", text)
        if op_match:
            op = {"and": "&&", "or": "||", ",": ","}.get(op_match.group("op"))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Couldn't parse '{text}'!")
        text = text[op_match.end() :].strip()
        f_token2 = text_to_filter(text)
        if isinstance(f_token2, ComplexFilter):
            # noinspection PyTypeChecker
            return ComplexFilter(f_token, op, f_token2)
        if isinstance(f_token2, FilterList) and f_token2.op == op:
            if op == ",":
                return f_token + f_token2
            elif op == "&&":
                return f_token & f_token2
            elif op == "||":
                return f_token | f_token2
            raise ValueError(f"Couldn't parse '{text}'!")
        elif isinstance(f_token2, FilterList):
            # noinspection PyTypeChecker
            return ComplexFilter(f_token, op, f_token2)
        if isinstance(f_token2, F):
            # noinspection PyTypeChecker
            return FilterList(f_token, f_token2, op=op)

def get_vdom_scope(self, vdom: str) -> Optional[Scope]:
    """Get Scope for a VDOM to be used by filters

    Returns:
        (Scope or None): The scope for the given VDOM
    """
    if vdom in (s_vdom.name for s_vdom in self.vdom):
        return Scope(name=self.name, vdom=vdom)
    return None

def get_url(self, method="get") -> str:
    """Derive URL for object based on initial URL fields

    Returns:
        URL string to call
    """
    url = FMGBaseObject.get_url(self, method)
    if self.interface is None:
        raise FMGException("interface field is required!")
    url = url.replace("{interface}", self.interface)
    if self.dynamic_mapping_name is None and self.dynamic_mapping_vdom is None:
        url = url.replace("/{dynamic_mapping_name}/{dynamic_mapping_vdom}", "")
    elif self.dynamic_mapping_name and self.dynamic_mapping_vdom:
        url = url.replace("{dynamic_mapping_name}", self.dynamic_mapping_name)
        url = url.replace("{dynamic_mapping_vdom}", self.dynamic_mapping_vdom)
    else:
        raise FMGException("dynamic_mapping_name and dynamic_mapping_vdom both are required!")
    return url

    """Derive URL for object based on initial URL fields

    Returns:
        URL string to call
    """
    url = FMGBaseObject.get_url(self, method)
    if self.interface is None:

def get_fmg_error(error_code: Union[str, int]) -> Optional[Union[Type[FMGException], str]]:
    """FMG API error code lookup

High-level synchronous FortiManager client.

Accepts configuration models and execution objects, constructs API requests, and returns bound models from high-level GET operations. Dictionary requests remain supported for endpoints without models. Use an authenticated connection context for object operations.

def __init__(self, settings: Optional[FMGSettings] = None, **kwargs):
    """Initialize the FortiManager client

    Args:
        settings (FMGSettings): Connection settings; when supplied, takes precedence over keyword settings

    Keyword Args:
        base_url (str): Base URL to access FMG (e.g.: https://myfmg)
        username (str): User to authenticate
        password (str): Password for authentication
        adom (str): ADOM to use for this connection
        verify (bool): Verify SSL certificate (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE can set accepted CA cert)
        timeout (float): Connect/read inactivity timeout per transport attempt, in seconds
        raise_on_error (bool): Raise exception on error
        discard_on_close (bool): Discard changes after connection close (workspace mode)
        discard_on_error (bool): Discard changes when exception occurs (workspace mode)
    """
    super().__init__(settings, **kwargs)
    self._async_context: Optional[AsyncFMG] = None

@error_handling
def add(self, request: MULTI_REQUEST_ARG) -> FMGResponse:
    """Create configuration objects in FortiManager.

    Args:
        request: One model or dictionary, or a nonempty list containing only models or only dictionaries.

    Returns:
        FMGResponse: Operation status; read the object separately to obtain its resulting configuration.

    Notes:
        This operation writes configuration. Models use API aliases and omit None values.
        Empty lists are sent explicitly. Batch operations are not a transaction; partial writes
        may remain after a failure. Check firmware semantics before using SET for a resource.

    Examples:
        Inside an open connection, with the appropriate target and permissions:

        ```python
        from pyfortinet.fmg_api.firewall import Address

        address = Address(name="example-server", subnet="192.0.2.10/32")
        response = fmg.add(address)
        ```
    """
    request = prepare_batch(request, allow_objects=True)
    if isinstance(request[0], dict):  # dict input, low-level operation
        return super().add(request)
    elif isinstance(request[0], FMGObject):  # high-level operation

            )
        return super().add(request=api_data)

def clone(self, request: REQUEST_ARG, *, create_task: bool = False, **new: str) -> FMGResponse:
    """Clone one configuration object using new identity values.

    Args:
        request: Source model or raw clone request dictionary.
        create_task: Request a background task. Keep the connection open until it finishes.
        **new: New identity fields, usually name, matching the model's master keys.

    Returns:
        FMGResponse: Clone operation status, with task metadata when provided by FortiManager.

    Examples:
        Inside an open connection, clone an existing address to an unused name:

        ```python
        from pyfortinet.fmg_api.firewall import Address

        response = fmg.clone(Address(name="example-server"), name="example-server-copy")
        ```
    """
    response = FMGResponse(fmg=self)
    if isinstance(request, dict):  # JSON input, low-level operation
        return super().clone(request, create_task=create_task)
    elif isinstance(request, FMGObject):  # high-level operation
        if not request.master_keys:
            raise FMGMissingMasterKeyException(f"Need to specify a master key for {request}")
        # master_key = first(request.master_keys.values())  # assume one master_key, like `name`
        # master_value = getattr(request, master_key)
        request.fmg_scope = request.fmg_scope or self._settings.adom
        return super().clone(
            {
                "url": request.get_url(method="clone"),
                "data": new,
            },
            create_task=create_task,
        )
    else:
        response.data = {"error": f"Wrong type of request received: {request}"}
        response.status = 400
        logger.error(response.data["error"])
        if self._raise_on_error:
            raise FMGWrongRequestException(request)
        return response

def exec(self, request: Union[dict[str, Any], FMGExecObject]) -> FMGResponse:
    """Execute on FMG"""
    if isinstance(request, dict):  # low-level operation
        return super().exec(request)
    elif isinstance(request, FMGExecObject):
        logger.info("requesting exec with high-level op to %s", request.get_url())
        request.fmg_scope = request.fmg_scope or self._settings.adom
        return super().exec({"url": request.get_url(), "data": request.data})
    else:
        result = FMGResponse(fmg=self, data=[{"error": f"Wrong type of request received: {request}"}])
        if self._raise_on_error:
            raise FMGWrongRequestException(result.data[0]["error"])
        return result
